sections.title: How poverty is measured
sections.summary: Thresholds, programme guidelines and the time spent in poverty

blocks.text: These reference tables identify the measure, income year, geographic scope and population before a statistic is used in the report. Census thresholds, HHS guidelines and the Supplemental Poverty Measure answer different questions.

The historical SIPP data follow the same respondents across months. The 2011–2012 and 2013–2014 observations span 24 months; 2017–2019 spans 36. National published editions are shown separately, with later source corrections recorded in the working-source notes.

sections.title: Official poverty thresholds, 2024
sections.summary: The complete Census grid in annual dollars

blocks.text: The applicable threshold depends on family size, related children under 18 and, for one- or two-person units, age. The same statistical thresholds apply across the country. An empty table cell is not applicable.

For a four-person family with two related children under 18, the 2024 threshold is $31,812. This statistical threshold measures poverty; the self-sufficiency chapter separately models the cost of basic needs.

sections.title: HHS guidelines for the 2024 reference year
sections.summary: The contiguous-states schedule used for Ohio

blocks.text: The 2024 HHS schedule for the contiguous states and DC is $31,200 for a four-person family or household. It is a separately published administrative guideline. Programmes define the relevant income, family and effective date; this historical table does not determine a person’s eligibility.
For more than eight people, the 2024 contiguous-states schedule adds $5,380 per additional person. The editable source also retains the separately published Alaska and Hawaii schedules.

sections.title: Official and supplemental poverty measures
sections.summary: Units, resources, thresholds and the population being measured

blocks.text: The Supplemental Poverty Measure adds selected noncash resources, deducts necessary expenses and adjusts for housing tenure and location. The official measure uses pretax cash income. Their population universes also differ, which is why direct Census comparisons use the official+ convention.

sections.title: Published poverty dynamics by observation period

blocks.text: Episodic poverty is a spell of at least two consecutive months during the observation period. Chronic poverty means poverty in every month of that period. People in chronic poverty are included in the episodic measure.

The following tables reproduce historical published editions. Census subsequently corrected Social Security income processing in the underlying data. The accompanying source register distinguishes those editions, the February 2024 annual/monthly replacement tables and the July 2025 fixed microdata.
The 24-month and 36-month columns have different observation windows. Their rates are not presented as a single comparable time trend, and all figures in this chapter refer to the United States.

Each sample requires participation across its full 24 months. The source holds demographic characteristics at the beginning of the period. Counts, original confidence intervals and edition details remain editable with every row.

Age is measured as of December 2019. Education categories cover adults age 25 and older. Race and Hispanic-origin categories can overlap. These are the original Figure 5 rates and retain the source’s processing-correction notice.
